title: Transitivity chain conflates the KMP refinement ladder into kmp2_correct
intent: Collapse the three-step refinement chain kmp2 ≤ kmp1 ≤ kmp ≤ kmp_SPEC into one headline correctness theorem `kmp2_correct` by transitivity, so the final KMP implementation is shown correct without restating the intermediate refinement proofs.

parent.name: kmp2_correct
parent.statement:
lemma kmp2_correct: "s \<noteq> []
  \<Longrightarrow> kmp2 s t \<le> kmp_SPEC s t"

children.name: kmp2_refine
children.statement: lemma kmp2_refine: "kmp2 s t \<le> kmp1 s t"
children.closed_by: apply (rule refine_IdD), then refine_rcg/refine_dref_type then auto
children.note: Replaces the abstract compute_\<ff>s_SPEC with the executable compute_butlast_\<ff>s in kmp2.

children.name: kmp1_refine
children.statement: lemma kmp1_refine: "kmp1 s t \<le> kmp s t"
children.closed_by: apply (rule refine_IdD), intro ASSERT_refine_right/left, intro_spec_refine, refine_rcg/refine_dref_type then auto
children.note: Introduces the stored-\<ff> optimisation: kmp1 computes the \<ff>-values once up front instead of on the fly.

children.name: kmp_correct
children.statement:
lemma kmp_correct: "s \<noteq> []
  \<Longrightarrow> kmp s t \<le> kmp_SPEC s t"
children.closed_by: refine_vcg with two WHILEIT termination measures, then six subgoals closed by metis/blast/simp/fastforce/auto
children.note: The naive, non-evaluable kmp algorithm refines the specification kmp_SPEC under the precondition s ≠ [].

applicability.goal_shape: A refinement goal `A s t ≤ B s t` (an ≤ inequality of `nres` nondeterminism monads) that decomposes into a transitive chain `A ≤ C ≤ … ≤ B`, where each single step is already proved as its own named refinement lemma.
applicability.use_when: You already hold each single-step refinement as its own lemma (`kmp2_refine`, `kmp1_refine`, `kmp_correct` here) and want one headline correctness theorem without restating the intermediate proofs; the steps are all `≤` inequalities so Isar's `also`/`finally` (transitivity) chains them with no extra work.
applicability.avoid_when: Any step is not yet proved as a named lemma (the chain cannot close by `(fact …)` and you must inline or prove the gap); the steps are not all the same relation (Isar's `also` does not compose `≥` by default); or a step's hypothesis needs discharging at the use site (here `kmp_correct` needs `s ≠ []`, supplied as `kmp_correct[OF ‹s ≠ []›]`).

claims.claim: The parent site `kmp2_correct` is 9 lines long.
The parent site `kmp2_correct` cites the lemma `kmp1_refine`.
The lemma `kmp_correct` is declared at lines 476-490 of thys/examples/KMP.thy.

The authors note that `kmp2_refine`'s proof is trivial because `compute_butlast_\<ff>s_refine` carries the `[refine]` attribute: "Using compute_butlast_\<ff>s_refine (it has attribute refine), the proof is trivial".

metrics.how_counted: three inequalities kmp2 ≤ kmp1, kmp1 ≤ kmp, kmp ≤ kmp_SPEC, each closed by `(fact …)` in lines 877-879 of the copied file

consequences: The move transfers the head step's precondition (`s ≠ []`) into the final theorem, and each `also` link must be a named lemma or fact, applied as `by (fact …)`. The chain is only as strong as its weakest link: if any intermediate refinement lemma is later weakened, the conflation breaks and must be re-checked. Obligations: every link must be an inequality in the same relation so `also`/`finally` (transitivity) applies, and the first step's assumptions must be supplied at the use site (`kmp_correct[OF ‹s ≠ []›]`).
